subject: crab
pitch: A feisty red rock crab with one oversized claw raised in challenge. A wide, knobbly shell in brick red speckled with orange and cream, eyes on stalks, eight jointed walking legs with pointed tips, and claws with dark tips and little teeth on the pinchers. A tiny barnacle and a strand of seaweed cling to the back of its shell.
reasoning:
I'm planning the TypeScript module structure using the SDK, setting up a crab model with a root body joint positioned above the floor so the legs reach the ground, then building out the shell and limb components.

For the shell, I'm shaping it as a squashed sphere with scale adjustments for width and flatness, giving it a brick-red speckled paint texture with lighter spots scattered across the surface, plus small bumpy knobs added via scattering on the shell surface. I'm also adding eye stalks as rods connecting the body to small eye spheres, and planning eight legs in four pairs using chain paths swept into tubes.

I'm working out the leg structure using hip joints attached to the body, with each leg built as a chain of points (thigh, shin, foot segments) swept into tapered tubes that come to a point at the foot, using a polyline path with named segments matching the joint count.

For the crab's pose, I'm positioning four legs per side splayed outward and downward to the floor, with staggered z-positions along the body, and tapering the tip radius to zero so the foot comes to a fine point. I'm also laying out the claw arm as a chain from shoulder to elbow to wrist to claw base, planning to build the pincer itself as two separate extruded halves.

Now I'm sketching the pincer profiles as tapered rod sweeps with small cone-shaped teeth along the inner edge, computed via simple lerp between hand-picked points, plus a tiny barnacle detail near the shoulder.

Placing seaweed by finding the nearest point on the shell surface and sweeping a wavy taper from that hit point, adding a few leaf slabs as flat polygons offset from the base rather than textured cards.

For knobs, I'm scattering small sphere studs across the shell surface with a minimum distance and a filter favoring upward-facing normals, then sinking each sphere slightly into the surface using an embed fraction so they look partially sunk rather than floating. I'm sizing and positioning the crab shell as a scaled sphere (wide and flattened) anchored near the body joint so its underside clears the hip height where legs attach, then setting up a spot paint pattern on top.

For coloring, I'm layering a countershade base (darker back, lighter belly) under a spot pattern for the shell, with darker tones for legs, reddish claws with dark tips, and eye stalks topped by pale eyeballs with small dark pupils. I'm defining the body as the root joint, explicitly binding parts to it with a bone reference to avoid ambiguous attachment, then building leg chains parented to the body with role "leg" and appropriate joint names matching the polyline points, before sweeping tubes along each chain with rounded or pointed end caps for the leg segments.

Tapering the radius function toward zero near the tips so the point caps render cleanly without artifacts, and keeping the tip radius small enough that it barely touches the floor plane without visibly sinking in. Now I'm setting up the mirrored leg geometry — defining a signed-side function so I can generate both left and right legs symmetrically, with hip, knee, ankle, and tip points fanned out with forward/backward z-offsets for that crab-like splayed stance.

I'm checking that the hip joints land close to the body shell's surface so legs appear to emerge naturally from the torso rather than floating outside it, adjusting the outward z-offsets per leg for the fan pattern. Then I'm moving on to defining the claw arm chain — shoulder, elbow, and wrist joint positions on just the left side, setting up the joint names for the sweep chain.

Now I'm sketching the pincer geometry: two tapered sweeps branching from the wrist joint, one forming the upper pincer and one the lower, with slightly different polyline paths so the claw looks open and raised, using a radius function that tapers from wide at the base to a sharp point at the tip.

For the dark claw tips, I'm reusing each pincer's same path but cropping it to the last quarter with a darker color so it reads as a contrasting tip, keeping the caps pointed for a sharp look. Then I'm adding small teeth-like spikes along the inner edge of the upper pincer, positioning their base points roughly along the polyline and angling them inward and downward so they look like serrations.

Still working out claw details... I'm now adding a second, smaller claw on the other side for the crab's smaller nipper, scaling down the same pincer function with a smaller radius and shifted position, then planning eye stalks as thin rods topped with small spheres positioned at the front of the shell.

Now I'm placing the pupils just slightly forward of the eye spheres, checking shell height to position the stalk bases correctly inside the shell surface, and adding a small barnacle cone embedded on the back of the shell along with a seaweed piece swept from a point near it using a wavy polyline path.

Still building seaweed geometry...

For the shell texture, I'm scattering knobs in alternating orange and cream colors across the upper half of the surface using a filter on the hit position, and painting the legs a solid rust-brown color.

For the legs, I'm building each one as a chain of points swept with a tapering radius, anchored at the hip inside the shell, making sure each joint name uses only letters, digits, and underscores to satisfy the naming rules.

Still writing paint setup...

Adding scattered knobs on top...

Adding seaweed next, sweeping a tapered strand from a root point near the shell up through a curved path with shrinking width, checking that mixing hit points and raw coordinate arrays in the path still type-checks fine since both qualify as valid point inputs.

Then I'm sketching leaves as flat triangular slabs with a leafy green color, and planning the crab's eye stalks as tapered rods ending in white spheres with dark pupils, making sure each part has the required color and bone attachment options specified correctly.

For the claws, I'm designing a reusable function that builds both a large left pincer and smaller right pincer by mirroring arm joint positions across the x-axis, then computing the upper and lower pincer segments as offsets from the wrist position scaled by a size factor.

Still defining pincer geometry...

Adjusting pincer offsets so the gap stays visible, then adding small spike-based teeth near the upper mid point with a couple offset positions for variation.

Now I'm defining the mirrored tooth direction, confirming it stays symmetrical, then setting up leg geometry with hip, knee, ankle, and tip coordinates across four z-offsets for front-to-back leg placement.

Each leg becomes a three-segment chain (hip, knee, foot) parented to the body with floor contact at the tip, and I'm placing eye stalks with rod coloring near the front. I'm double-checking imports, geometry helpers, and the shell surface binding before writing out the final exported code.
